messages.subject: derivation of Cholesky-based cov matrix in doc
parts:
I put the derivation of the transform and unconstrained
transform with absolute Jacobian determinant into the
doc, the source for which is in:

/stan/doc/manuals/gm.tex

(See note below on generating the pdf.)

I'm pretty confident in my derivation this time, but
would still appreciate a second set of eyes giving it a look
before I code it.

The punchline is that the transform involves:

- K exponential functions,
- (K x K) Cholesky factor product

and its log absolute Jacobian determinant involves:

- 1 + K + (K * K) additions
- (K * K) logs

Does anyone know the complexity of the
Cholesky factor product? I'm afraid it'll be
O(K^3) like ordinary matrix products, but was hoping
all the missing terms reduced the order. The logs
and exponents will probably dominate at low orders (K < 20)
anyway.

Note: Remember that if you don't have the Lucida fonts installed
then you'll have to follow the instructions
at the very top of gm.tex and do a little editing to get
it to run pdflatex with built-in Times Roman + AMS Fonts.
I don't know if there's a legal, free way to get the
Lucida fonts installed. I went with the $99 package
a while back when I was writing a manual for our company.

- Bob

On Wednesday, April 4, 2012 2:53:18 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I put the derivation of the transform and unconstrained
transform with absolute Jacobian determinant into the
doc, the source for which is in:

   /stan/doc/manuals/gm.tex

(See note below on generating the pdf.)

I'm pretty confident in my derivation this time, but
would still appreciate a second set of eyes giving it a look
before I code it.

The punchline is that the transform involves:

    - K exponential functions,
    - (K x K) Cholesky factor product

and its log absolute Jacobian determinant involves:

    - 1 + K + (K * K) additions
    - (K * K) logs
The code wouldn't have to take those logs in practice if you evaluate the Jacobian determinant part before you set the diagonal of L.

Does anyone know the complexity of the
Cholesky factor product?  I'm afraid it'll be
O(K^3) like ordinary matrix products, but was hoping
all the missing terms reduced the order.  The logs
and exponents will probably dominate at low orders (K < 20)
anyway.

Both taking a Cholesky decomposition and the L * L' operation are O(K^3), just with a lower constant than a lot of O(K^3) operations. Note that Eigen does not have a fully optimized way of  calculating L * L' (like BLAS does) so we may have to do some experimentation to see what goes fastest in stan. You can either take advantage of symmetry or take advantage of the fact that L is triangular, but not both as of the last time I checked. But the main point is that rarely would you have to take a Cholesky decomposition (maybe once at the beginning) or calculate L * L' (because you usually only need L).

Ben
